unit.why: A short memorate, heard from R. Moshe Teitelbaum, describing how R. Shmelke habitually prayed on Shabbat and holidays with kavvanot and sang wondrous new melodies while cleaving to the upper world. It depicts habitual conduct, not a single event, so it is a borderline narrative.
unit.boundary_note: Shvachim of R. Shmelke run across neighbouring divisions; this is a self-contained excerpt from Yetiv Panim.

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ ייטיב פנים מאמר שפת הים
stories.summary_en: R. Moshe Teitelbaum relates that R. Shmelke, praying on Shabbat, festivals and especially the Days of Awe, meditated on kavvanot between the words and, in rapt cleaving to the upper world, sang wondrous new melodies without knowing what he sang.
